cards.power: Indecision. Flip a coin. If heads, do nothing. If tails, write a poem about doing nothing.
cards.lore: O, that this too too solid flesh would melt... or at least nap.
cards.gradeReason: Writing a poem about doing nothing IS the action. Instant table gold.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ink-washed storybook. Subject: Melancholy basset hound in black cape, rainy backdrop. Mood: Theatrical despair.

cards.power: Usurp. Swap hands with the player who has the most points.
cards.lore: A brother's murder. Pray can I not. My stronger guilt defeats my strong intent.
cards.gradeReason: Usurp is exactly what Claudius does. Perfect mechanic-character alignment.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Regal grotesque watercolor. Subject: Rat in crown holding poison bottle. Mood: Guilty grandeur.

cards.power: Willful Ignorance. Ignore the effects of the next Action Card played against you.
cards.lore: The lady doth protest too much, methinks.
cards.gradeReason: Clever but passive — player knows what to do, not what to BE.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Elegant ink portrait. Subject: Pampered white poodle with wine glass, oblivious expression. Mood: Willfully serene.

cards.power: Haunt. Force an opponent to discard their highest card.
cards.lore: I am thy father's spirit... doom'd for a certain term to walk the night.
cards.gradeReason: Ghost steals the best thing you have — mechanically perfect haunting.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Pen-and-ink gothic. Subject: Dog-shaped ghost in white sheet, glowing eyes. Mood: Mournful vengeance.

cards.power: Verbose. Talk uninterrupted for 30 seconds. If anyone interrupts, draw a card.
cards.lore: Brevity is the soul of wit... and tediousness the limbs and outward flourishes.
cards.gradeReason: Talking for 30 seconds while quoting Polonius IS the card. Pure performance.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Victorian pen comic. Subject: Pompous parrot in courtly robes gesturing theatrically. Mood: Self-important bombast.

cards.power: Distraction. Sing a song. Opponents must cover their ears or lose a turn.
cards.lore: Lord, we know what we are, but know not what we may be.
cards.gradeReason: Singing at the table until opponents submit — that's immediate joyful chaos.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Soft watercolor. Subject: Otter floating with flowers, singing, dreamy expression. Mood: Melancholy enchantment.

cards.power: Revenge. Deal double damage to any player who played a 'Hamlet' card.
cards.lore: I dare damnation. To this point I stand... only I'll be reveng'd.
cards.gradeReason: Revenge double-damage vs Hamlet cards — mechanically brutal, thematically perfect.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Aggressive woodblock print. Subject: Rooster in dueling pose, feathers bristling. Mood: Furious honor.

cards.power: Witness. If you lose the game, you may narrate the winner's victory to make them feel guilty.
cards.lore: Absent thee from felicity awhile... to tell my story.
cards.gradeReason: Consolation prize with narrative power — clever but needs a losing player to trigger.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Dignified portrait style. Subject: Golden retriever with journal, watching from sidelines. Mood: Loyal melancholy.

cards.power: Memento Mori. All players must discard all 'Vanity' cards.
cards.lore: A fellow of infinite jest... where be your gibes now?
cards.gradeReason: Holding a skull and nuking vanity cards — the mechanic IS the Shakespeare bit.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Dark baroque ink. Subject: Skull with worm emerging, jester hat nearby. Mood: Nihilistic comedy.

cards.power: Expendable. You may discard this card to avoid taking damage.
cards.lore: They are not near my conscience.
cards.gradeReason: Named Expendable and used as a shield — the joke lands the moment you read it.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Duo portrait comedy. Subject: Two identical hamsters in Elizabethan ruffs, confused expressions. Mood: Cheerful futility.

cards.power: Guilt Trip. Look at an opponent's hand. If they have a 'King' card, they must discard it.
cards.lore: The play's the thing wherein I'll catch the conscience of the king.
cards.gradeReason: Catching a King card with a play mechanic — cleanest lore-mechanic lock in the deck.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Tiny theatre illustration. Subject: Mice in costume performing on stage, king mouse watching nervously. Mood: Theatrical accusation.

cards.power: Accidental Death. Pass this card to the left. That player loses 5 HP.
cards.lore: The drink, the drink! I am poison'd.
cards.gradeReason: Hot-potato damage card with Gertrude's last words — instant dread at the table.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Gothic still life. Subject: Ornate goblet with green vapor rising, skull reflection. Mood: Elegant dread.

cards.power: Ambition. Gain +10 Power, but you cannot sleep (skip your draw phase).
cards.lore: I am in blood stepp'd in so far... returning were as tedious as go o'er.
cards.gradeReason: Gain everything, lose rest — the Macbeth bargain executed perfectly.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Menacing expressionist. Subject: Hyena in tartan cloak, crazed upward gaze, bloody daggers. Mood: Feverish ambition.

cards.power: Coercion. Force another player to attack a target of your choice.
cards.lore: Out, damned spot! out, I say!
cards.gradeReason: She makes others do the dirty work — Lady Macbeth as a mechanic, flawless.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Sinister elegant portrait. Subject: Hairless Sphynx cat in black gown, pointing imperiously. Mood: Icy command.

cards.power: Prophecy. Look at the top 3 cards of the deck. Arrange them to screw over your friends.
cards.lore: Double, double toil and trouble; Fire burn and cauldron bubble.
cards.gradeReason: Seeing the future and weaponizing it against friends is the witches in one move.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Grotesque folk art. Subject: Three toads in robes stirring cauldron, cackling. Mood: Gleeful malice.

cards.power: Guilt. The player with the most cards cannot play any Actions this turn.
cards.lore: Thou canst not say I did it; never shake thy gory locks at me.
cards.gradeReason: Guilt mechanic targets the leader — clever but needs you to track hand sizes.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ethereal portrait. Subject: Bloodied grey hound apparition at banquet table. Mood: Accusatory haunting.

cards.power: Not Born of Woman. Defeat any card with the 'Tyrant' tag automatically.
cards.lore: Macduff was from his mother's womb untimely ripp'd.
cards.gradeReason: Auto-defeat tyrants is satisfying but needs Tyrant tags in play to shine.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Heroic battle etching. Subject: Ram in full armor charging forward, loophole banner. Mood: Righteous fury.

cards.power: Innocence. If this card is destroyed, the attacker loses 10 Reputation.
cards.lore: Poor bird! thou'ldst never fear the net nor lime.
cards.gradeReason: Defensive martyrdom — powerful but only activates on death, passive until then.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Soft tragic illustration. Subject: Nesting bird with dark shadow looming overhead. Mood: Fragile innocence.

cards.power: Comic Relief. Pause the game. Everyone takes a drink.
cards.lore: Drink, sir, is a great provoker of three things... nose-painting, sleep, and urine.
cards.gradeReason: Pausing a card game so everyone drinks is a perfect real-world kayfabe moment.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Pub cartoon. Subject: Jovial badger holding a pint, HELL sign on door behind him. Mood: Bawdy relief.

cards.power: Restoration. Shuffle the discard pile back into the deck.
cards.lore: Pour we in our country's purge each drop of us.
cards.gradeReason: Resetting the deck is useful — Malcolm as deck-restorer is thematically apt but quiet.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Heraldic illustration. Subject: Young lamb in armor holding a Scotland banner. Mood: Hopeful restoration.

cards.power: Hallucination. Reroll your attack dice. If you fail, you attack yourself.
cards.lore: Is this a dagger which I see before me, the handle toward my hand?
cards.gradeReason: Reroll or stab yourself — Macbeth's madness as a risk mechanic is chef's kiss.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Surreal impressionist. Subject: Floating glowing dagger above outstretched anxious paw. Mood: Paranoid vision.

cards.power: Camouflage. Your units cannot be targeted this turn.
cards.lore: And now a wood comes toward Dunsinane.
cards.gradeReason: Untargetable turn is clean — but it's a standard protection effect missing a performance hook.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Eerie forest illustration. Subject: Trees with legs marching through mist toward castle. Mood: Uncanny advance.

cards.power: Brew. Sacrifice two weak cards to summon one strong card.
cards.lore: Cool it with a baboon's blood, then the charm is firm and good.
cards.gradeReason: Sacrifice ritual mechanic — players lean in, quote the witches, it's theatrical.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Alchemical woodcut. Subject: Bubbling cauldron with frog and strange ingredients, green glow. Mood: Arcane brew.

cards.power: Insomnia. No players may 'Rest' or heal this turn.
cards.lore: Macbeth does murder sleep, the innocent sleep.
cards.gradeReason: Denying healing is solid — Sleep as a card name is evocative but the effect is passive.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Disturbed dream illustration. Subject: Pillow with knife wound, blood-red sheets. Mood: Violated innocence.

cards.power: Abdicate. Give half your cards to two other players. Then scream at them.
cards.lore: I am a man more sinn'd against than sinning.
cards.gradeReason: Give away your power THEN scream at the people who took it — King Lear as a mechanic.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Stormy oil-painting style. Subject: Aged lion in torn robes screaming at storm. Mood: Magnificent ruin.

cards.power: Truth Bomb. Reveal an opponent's hand. Mock their strategy.
cards.lore: The fool will stay, and let the wise man fly.
cards.gradeReason: Reveal AND mock — the mandatory mockery is what makes this a performance card.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Jester portrait. Subject: Bright bird in motley costume waving a bladder stick. Mood: Incisive wit.

cards.power: Eviction. Force a player to discard a 'Land' or 'Home' card.
cards.lore: I'll not chide thee... thou art a boil, a plague sore.
cards.gradeReason: Stealing land is thematic — but needs the right card type in play to land.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Cold portrait. Subject: Vulture in fine dress pointing imperiously. Mood: Calculating cruelty.

cards.power: Cruelty. Select a player. That player is now 'Blind' (plays cards face down).
cards.lore: Prescribe not us our duty.
cards.gradeReason: Blind mechanic is disorienting and fun — but 'Blind' status needs table-level trust to enforce.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Cruel elegance. Subject: Cobra in regal robes, cold eyes, one fang exposed. Mood: Aristocratic venom.

cards.power: Despair. Roll a die. If 1-3, jump off the cliff (discard hand). If 4-6, survive miraculously.
cards.lore: I have no way, and therefore want no eyes.
cards.gradeReason: Dice-based cliff jump is dramatic but requires knowing the cliff flavor — one step from G1.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Tragic comedy. Subject: Blind mole at clifftop, arms spread, uncertain footing. Mood: Desperate dignity.

cards.power: Bastard's Ambition. Swap your lowest card for an opponent's highest card.
cards.lore: Now, gods, stand up for bastards!
cards.gradeReason: The lore is a battle cry and the power is pure ambition — play it loud or go home.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Scheming portrait. Subject: Sleek fox in half-open coat holding a forged letter, sly grin. Mood: Audacious cunning.

cards.power: Disguise. You cannot be targeted by attacks this turn.
cards.lore: Tom's acold... The foul fiend bites my back.
cards.gradeReason: Standard protection in disguise framing — thematically right, mechanically quiet.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Ragged pen sketch. Subject: Scruffy dog in torn disguise, hunched on moor. Mood: Desperate concealment.

cards.power: Bluntness. Cancel a 'Flattery' or 'Persuasion' effect.
cards.lore: Sir, 'tis my occupation to be plain.
cards.gradeReason: Counter-flattery is satisfying if the effect is in play — depends on meta.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Gruff character study. Subject: Stocky bulldog in plain coat, arms crossed, no-nonsense expression. Mood: Steadfast loyalty.

cards.power: Cataclysm. All players discard 1 card for every card they hold.
cards.lore: Blow, winds, and crack your cheeks! rage! blow!
cards.gradeReason: Mass discard with a Shakespeare scream — the lore demands you deliver the line.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Dramatic weather illustration. Subject: Howling storm clouds with lightning striking a moor. Mood: Apocalyptic fury.

cards.power: Humiliation. Choose a player. They lose their next turn.
cards.lore: Fortune, that arrant whore, ne'er turns the key to th' poor.
cards.gradeReason: Skip-turn with a humiliation frame — needs the table to commit to the roasting.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Medieval comedy woodcut. Subject: Chicken locked in stocks, looking dejected. Mood: Public shame.

cards.power: Placebo. Heal 5 HP even though nothing actually happened.
cards.lore: Ten masts at each make not the altitude which thou hast perpendicularly fell.
cards.gradeReason: Healing via imaginary fall is wonderfully absurd — works well if players know the bit.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Absurdist landscape. Subject: Bunny standing on gentle slope imagining it's a cliff. Mood: Ridiculous self-deception.

cards.power: Tragic End. The game ends immediately. Everyone loses.
cards.lore: Why should a dog, a horse, a rat, have life, and thou no breath at all?
cards.gradeReason: Nuclear 'everyone loses' button — the ultimate kayfabe sacrifice card.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Sorrowful oil-painting. Subject: White dove lying still in Lear's paws, rain falling. Mood: Devastating grief.

cards.power: Infinite Variety. Change the rules of the game for one turn.
cards.lore: Age cannot wither her, nor custom stale her infinite variety.
cards.gradeReason: Rewrite the rules for a turn — Cleopatra's power is EXACTLY this and it's G1.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Opulent Art Nouveau. Subject: Peacock-snake hybrid on golden throne, commanding posture. Mood: Mesmerizing sovereignty.

cards.power: Dotage. Ignore your responsibilities. Lose 5 Defense, Gain 5 Charisma.
cards.lore: The triple pillar of the world transform'd into a strumpet's fool.
cards.gradeReason: Trade defense for charisma — thematically perfect, mechanically needs table to run Charisma rules.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Faded glory portrait. Subject: Aging war horse in toga drinking wine, medals tarnished. Mood: Magnificent decline.

cards.power: Bureaucracy. Tax the other players. Take 1 Gold/Token from each.
cards.lore: He fishes, drinks, and wastes the lamps of night in revel.
cards.gradeReason: Tax mechanic is satisfying — needs the token economy to be live at table.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Corporate satire. Subject: Shark in Roman toga reviewing tax scrolls, cold eyes. Mood: Efficient cold control.

cards.power: Defection. Switch teams/alliances mid-battle. Die of heartbreak later.
cards.lore: The barge she sat in, like a burnish'd throne, burn'd on the water.
cards.gradeReason: 'Die of heartbreak later' is flavor text, not mechanic — needs that consequence built in.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Melancholy soldier portrait. Subject: Fox in soldier's cape turning away, head bowed. Mood: Regretful betrayal.

cards.power: Fortune Telling. Predict the next card drawn. If correct, keep it.
cards.lore: Let me be married to three kings in a forenoon, and widow them all.
cards.gradeReason: Prediction game is performative — needs confident delivery to pay off.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Luxurious Egyptian court. Subject: Two flamingos in gold jewelry reading tarot cards. Mood: Glamorous prophecy.

cards.power: Third Wheel. You exist. You do nothing effective. You are removed from the board easily.
cards.lore: What manner o' thing is your crocodile?
cards.gradeReason: Funny as a joke but literally no power — a card that self-describes uselessness.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Comic awkward portrait. Subject: Small crocodile in Roman toga standing between two larger figures, invisible. Mood: Irrelevant presence.

cards.power: Self-Sacrifice. Take damage intended for your Leader.
cards.lore: Thus do I escape the sorrow of Antony's death.
cards.gradeReason: Shield-bearer role is clear — but requires a Leader card on the board to trigger.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Loyal soldier sketch. Subject: Small dog in squire armor stepping in front of a blow. Mood: Selfless devotion.

cards.power: Bad News. The bearer of this card takes damage whenever a King/Queen dies.
cards.lore: The nature of bad news infects the teller.
cards.gradeReason: Passive curse mechanic — funny in concept, requires tracking deaths through the game.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Nervous courier illustration. Subject: Dog with sealed letter, looking over shoulder. Mood: Anxious dread.

cards.power: Quick Exit. Remove your Character from play without losing points.
cards.lore: With thy sharp teeth this knot intrinsicate of life at once untie.
cards.gradeReason: Honorable exit move is satisfying — Cleopatra's asp as an escape hatch is very on.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Miniature deadly still life. Subject: Tiny snake coiled in a fig basket, golden light. Mood: Peaceful fatality.

cards.power: Retreat. Flee the battle. Your reputation is destroyed.
cards.lore: The greater cantle of the world is lost with very ignorance.
cards.gradeReason: Flee for safety but lose reputation — solid trade, needs Reputation mechanic active.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Naval battle engraving. Subject: Warship turning away from battle in bathtub-sized sea. Mood: Shameful flight.

cards.power: Siege. You cannot be attacked for 2 turns, but you cannot attack either.
cards.lore: Lock yourself, and send him word you are dead.
cards.gradeReason: Full defensive lockout — survive by doing nothing, no performance hook whatsoever.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Stone fortress illustration. Subject: Locked stone tower with tiny figure peering out. Mood: Tactical paralysis.

cards.power: Debauchery. All players skip a turn to party.
cards.lore: In our own filth drop our clear judgments.
cards.gradeReason: Mass skip-to-party is chaotic fun — one step from G1 but lacks a performance trigger.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Roman party fresco style. Subject: Wine fountain overflowing, animals passed out around it. Mood: Glorious excess.

cards.power: A Plague on Both Houses. Deal damage to the two strongest players.
cards.lore: They have made worms' meat of me.
cards.gradeReason: The most quotable dying line in Shakespeare as a mechanic — you WILL say the line.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Dueling scene. Subject: Mongoose in rapier stance, wounded, mid-declaration. Mood: Defiant tragedy.

cards.power: Inception. Plant a false idea (card) in an opponent's hand.
cards.lore: She is the fairies' midwife... she gallops night by night through lovers' brains.
cards.gradeReason: Planting a false card in someone's hand is the dream-invader mechanic — G1 for creativity.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Miniature fairy tale. Subject: Tiny fairy-bug in hazelnut chariot speeding through dream clouds. Mood: Whimsical menace.

cards.power: Illusion. Cancel an attack; it was just a dream.
cards.lore: Begot of nothing but vain fantasy.
cards.gradeReason: Attack cancellation is useful — but 'it was just a dream' is flavor, not performance.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Surreal dream landscape. Subject: Castle dissolving into clouds, question mark hovering. Mood: Gossamer unreality.

cards.power: Transport. Move a card from the discard pile to your hand.
cards.lore: Made by the joiner squirrel or old grub.
cards.gradeReason: Discard retrieval is solid utility — the chariot frame is charming but low performance.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Tiny whimsy illustration. Subject: Squirrel piloting a walnut-shell chariot at high speed. Mood: Absurdly tiny adventure.

cards.power: Game Over. The player with the most 'Tragedy' points wins.
cards.lore: The rest is silence.
cards.gradeReason: Ending the game with Hamlet's last words — the lore IS the moment. No explanation needed.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Empty stage illustration. Subject: Bare theatre stage, scattered bodies, single spotlight. Mood: Final silence.

cards.power: Sudden Death. Eliminate one player instantly. No save.
cards.lore: This is the chase... I am gone for ever.
cards.gradeReason: The most famous stage direction in existence as an instant-kill. This card IS the deck.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Frantic cartoon chase. Subject: Terrified figure fleeing enormous bear offstage. Mood: Chaotic inevitability.

cards.power: Encore. Bring one character back from the dead (Discard pile).
cards.lore: That skull had a tongue in it, and could sing once.
cards.gradeReason: Resurrection from discard is good — works better if players track 'character' card types.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Morbid whimsy. Subject: Singing skull with musical notes floating in graveyard. Mood: Cheerful macabre.

cards.power: Chaos. Shuffle all hands together and redeal.
cards.lore: Stay Fluffy! KayfaBINGO!
cards.gradeReason: Total reset chaos is fun — but it's a meta-game intervention, not a Shakespeare bit.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Manic cartoon. Subject: FrizzleBob rabbit with huge grin giving thumbs up, cards exploding everywhere. Mood: Gleeful anarchy.

verdict: Shakespeare got suplexed and the Bard deserved every bit of it. Uncle FrizzleBob's Tragic Flaws is the strongest literary parody deck in the corpus — every character is a perfectly cast animal, every mechanic mirrors the tragedy it's named after. Exit, Pursued by a Bear as an instant-kill is the single best card in the Kayfabizarro canon. Minor weakness: the Antony & Cleopatra section has a run of passive mechanics (Defection heartbreak, Monument lockout, Lepidus being useless by design) that slow table energy compared to the Hamlet and Lear sequences. The Macbeth lore font artifacts (Courier Prime labels visible in text) are a cosmetic fix needed before Gumroad. Table-ready: YES.
blurb: For theater kids, Shakespeare nerds, and anyone who's ever wanted to eliminate a friend with a bear. 56 cards of tragic failure, animal casting, and kayfabe chaos — the Bard never had this much fun.

coverQA.coverVibeMatch: 5 — animal chaos + Elizabethan doom + FrizzleBob = perfectly coherent chaos
coverQA.coverViral: 4 — strong but slightly niche; 'Exit Pursued by a Bear' is the real viral hook inside
coverQA.coverNote: The cover leads with FrizzleBob's manifesto — 'Reality is for cowards. History is a lie.' — which is exactly the opening energy this deck earns. Shakespearean chaos rabbit is the correct mascot for the Bard's entire discography of catastrophic personal decisions. The HUBRIS mechanic card on the cover is a flex move that tells you everything about the design philosophy.

notes: 15 pages total: page 1 is cover/meta (4 explanatory cards), pages 2-15 are 56 playable cards in 2x2 grid. Covers Hamlet (pp.2-4), Macbeth (pp.5-7), King Lear (pp.8-10), Antony & Cleopatra (pp.11-13), Romeo & Juliet (pp.14), and universal epilogue cards (p.15). Font artifact: Macbeth section (cards 13-18, pages 5-6) labels lore as 'Lore (Courier Prime):' with font name visible in text — 6 cards affected. All cards have RAF dice boxes. Deck uses 'Slots: R:X | A:X | F:X' label notation in later pages (12-15) versus 'R:X | A:X | F:X' in earlier pages — minor label inconsistency. Lepidus is intentionally useless by design (self-aware joke card). The Mechanic: HUBRIS introduces a custom die-result rule that requires explanation before play.

marketingText:
Kayfabizarro: TRAGIC FLAWS – Shakespeare's Greatest Catastrophes, Recast as Animals Who Wrestle to the Death (Free Cut & Play Comic Card Game)

Every tragedy is one clever animal making a catastrophically stupid decision in front of witnesses.

Here is how the deck actually plays. You put down Hamlet and your power is indecision, so you flip a coin and on heads you do nothing at all. You put down Lear and you hand half your cards to two other players, then scream at them for taking it. You put down Macbeth and you gain ten power but you can never rest again, no draw phase, no relief. The rule is never bolted onto the character. The rule IS the character's fatal flaw, printed as a thing you have to perform out loud. That is the move the syllabus sands off: these people were not noble, they were disasters with excellent publicity, and the fastest way to actually feel a tragedy is to commit the bad call yourself and let the table watch it land.

This is Social Story Wrestling with the Bard's entire body count in one ring. You pick up a card, perform the flaw in character, and the room rules whether the scene holds or gets booked back behind the curtain. 56 cut-and-play cards casting Hamlet, Macbeth, Lear, and Antony and Cleopatra as animals who scheme, sulk, lie, and die exactly on cue.

WHAT'S INSIDE?
- The Tragic Flaws Core Deck: 56 High-Res "Print, Cut & Play" Cards, featuring Exit, Pursued by a Bear (eliminate one player on the spot with no save, while delivering the most famous stage direction in the language), Lear, The Old Lion (give half your hand to two rivals, then turn on them for having it), and Polonius, The Parrot (hold the table hostage for thirty uninterrupted seconds of courtly waffle, or anyone who cuts you off draws a card).
- The Freestyle Rules: the complete Anti-Rulebook. No complicated math, just storytelling, dice-driven chaos, and the HUBRIS die result that turns one overconfident swing into your own undoing the instant you reach too far.
- The Five-Tragedy Roster: every card belongs to its own catastrophe, from the Hamlet body-count to the toad-witches of Macbeth, the storm-blasted heath of Lear, and the doomed glamour of Antony and Cleopatra, closing on a universal epilogue where Exeunt Omnes hands the win to whoever hoarded the most tragedy and Uncle FrizzleBob's Approval shuffles every hand together and redeals the wreckage.

THE "LIVING DECK" PASS (Free Updates)
This is part of the FrizzleBob Shakespeare cycle. Grab it and you join the Komik Kard Kult Klub: every Othello, every Winter's Tale, every play still waiting for its animal cast arrives in your library as a free update, no second checkout, no expansion paywall.

WHY "PAY WHAT YOU WANT"?
I dig up dead playwrights and let strangers wrestle them at kitchen tables. Shakespeare wrote the funniest, cruelest, most quotable disasters in the language, and then four centuries of reverence taped his mouth shut and handed you a glossary instead of a folding chair. I make these so the tragedies stay dangerous and stay yours. Are you broke? Enter "0" and take it. Print it, cut it, run the bloodbath at your own table. Want to support the craft? Every dollar goes straight into the next deck and the next doomed cast.

Choose your reality. Become an Epistemic Outlaw.
"Shakespeare's heroes never died of fate. They died of one bad call, performed with total conviction."
Stay fluffy. — Uncle FrizzleBob
